claims.text: A defect-inclusive predictive approach will match measured conductivity significantly better than traditional perfect-crystal analytical models in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The proposed approach explicitly incorporates vacancies, interstitials, and oxygen impurities into electron and phonon transport simulations.
Vacancies, interstitials, and oxygen impurities modify the local atomic environment in HfNbTaTiZr.
These defects enhance electron and phonon scattering rates.
Defect-induced scattering changes carrier mobility and phonon mean free paths.
The changes in carrier mobility and phonon mean free path reduce conductivity relative to ideal-crystal predictions.
Temperature-activated phonon scattering is important in the 300–1200 K regime.
Quantum corrections to scattering are relevant in the 0–200 K regime.
The defect-inclusive model will predict conductivity approximately 10–20% below the perfect-crystal analytical prediction.
Adding 1 wt.% oxygen will cause additional scattering and lower conductivity relative to oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr.
Existing analytical predictions assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Existing analytical predictions overestimate conductivity because they omit additional electron and phonon scattering mechanisms.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with defect structures similar to those generated by standard arc-melting and homogenization.
The approach is applicable at oxygen concentrations up to approximately 1 wt.%.
The stated temperature applicability is limited to 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Outside the stated temperature ranges, phase transformations or oxidation kinetics may dominate transport behavior.
High vacuum during low-temperature testing avoids additional oxygen uptake.
An argon atmosphere during high-temperature testing prevents oxidation.
